sources.note: Synthesizes Cognitive Behavioral Therapy dialogues using a CoT strategy grounded in CBT guidelines plus a resistance orchestrator that steers simulated patients away from sycophantic compliance.
sources.title: ODRA: Synthesizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Sessions with Structured Chain-Of-Thought and Dynamic Patient Resistance

sources.note: A GRPO variant that teaches multimodal models to refuse when a referred object is absent, without losing localization accuracy on cases where it is present.
sources.title: Teaching MLLMs to Say No: Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension via Refusal Calibrated GRPO

sources.note: Fixes reward hacking in hybrid thinking/non-thinking RL by setting per-query token limits for non-thinking responses derived from the solution part of that query's thinking responses.
sources.title: Thinking-Based Non-Thinking: Solving the Reward Hacking Problem in Training Hybrid Reasoning Models via Reinforcement Learning

sources.note: Argues reasoning models' safety failures come from the reasoning structure itself, and achieves safety alignment by altering that structure with 1K supervised examples and no RL.
sources.title: Reasoning Structure Matters for Safety Alignment of Reasoning Models

sources.note: A competitive chess testbed where 13 models play each other, and no model beats a human-amateur-level engine while some lose to random play.
sources.title: ChessArena: A Chess Testbed for Evaluating Strategic Reasoning Capabilities of Large Language Models

sources.note: Keeps the LLM as the reasoner while a symbolic solver supplies a Logic-Augmented Context, so conflicts flagged by execution direct attention to violated constraints instead of replacing deduction.
sources.title: MAC-Reasoner: A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework for Enhancing Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models

sources.note: Separates reasoning into procedural advancement and 'epistemic verbalization' — the token-level externalization of uncertainty — and shows that emitting doubt is what lets a model recover from silent divergence, that injecting a bare doubt cue recovers failed trajectories, and that 800 SFT examples suffice to install or destroy the habit.
sources.title: Understanding Reasoning in LLMs through Strategic Information Allocation under Uncertainty

result.definition: Training on labelled input-output pairs, which seven sources use as the cheap baseline or the fallback when RL is too costly or too unstable. Two use it as the entire method — 1K examples to alter reasoning structure, and a chess-specific tune that brings an 8B model close to much larger reasoning models. Two use it downstream of something else, training on traces generated by a solver-verified pipeline or by a synthetic-dialogue framework. Two cite its cost as the reason to avoid it, one for hybrid-reasoning training and one for refusal calibration. The sources agree it is effective and disagree about whether its data cost or RL's instability is the greater problem.
